findings.text: the tail read is bounded to the last 64 KiB, so a run killed mid-turn whose final stream record is larger is read as having no last record and the death row never fires: measured at the reviewed head with a killed worker, an in-progress manifest and a real snapshot, a final record of about 64.5 KiB still yields row_state 'blocked' with the death clause while 65.5 KiB and 512 KiB yield last_record_type None, row_state 'working' and no death clause, which is the stale working column this node exists to replace; the small-record control fires, so the absence is the window and not the reader.
